newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after ECI data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after ECI data.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening higher on Tuesday after a report on the first quarter Employment Cost Index, a key gauge of wage inflation.
PHIL ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER OF VALUE LINE'S ASSET MANAGEMENT.
-- "This number's a blowout...This is materially slower thanexpected in terms of wage-cost inflation."

-- Said durable goods data was also weaker than expected. "It's fabulous number for the economy, we are definitely not running too hot and inflationary pressures viewed by some are simply non-existent. I think equities trade up on this, led primarily by the financial services companies."
The first quarter ECI rose 0.6 percent. According to a Reuters poll, economists had expected the ECI to be up 0.9 percent for the first quarter.
March durable goods orders fell 3.0 percent overall and fell 2.6 percent ex-defense, against a forecast for unchanged overall and a 0.1-percent drop ex-defense.
LARRY WACHTEL, ANALYST AT PRUDENTIAL SECURITIES:

-- "This is a very friendly number. Cause and effect says this is a benign number and bonds are rallying. Bonds are the gatekeeper for stocks. Yesterday the Street made a bet the numbers would be benign and the Street was right."
DICK STEIN, VICE PRESIDENT US CLEARING CORP:

-- "I thought it was great. Employment costs are well within confines. No one can get upset about that. I think this could get the market moving back to the upside. You could climb from where we closed yesterday. We could get back to the 6900 figure between now and the weekend."
-- "Financials will bounce sharply this morning. This will give backbone to a lot of people who have been on the sidelines."
GUY TRUICKO, PORTFOLIO MANAGER, UNITY MANAGEMENT:

-- "It should be a nice opening on the upside...(The data) are signs (the economy) is a little weaker than people were looking for...It's a busy week for data so the exictement will probably be muted."
The 30-year Treasury bond was up 1-8/32 to yield 7.02 percent.
